title: Battlefield
text: Battlefield Swiss-army toolkit designed define extract spatial spots specific regions spatial transcriptomics data.  provides low-level, modular utilities delineate spatial regions interest, including interfaces clusters, intra-cluster layers, andinter-cluster trajectories.  utilities intended reused composed within higher-level analytical workflows packages.  Battlefield supports sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics platforms as10x Genomics Visium, across multiple resolutions, including Visium HD (binned).

title: Battlefield
text: Battlefield provides four core functionalities define extract spatial transcriptomics spots specific tissue regions, enabling study spatial organization different biological contexts: Interfaces clusters — identify analyze boundary regions distinct tissue cell populations interact. Intra-cluster layers — characterize spatial layers gradients within single cluster. Inter/Intra-cluster trajectories — model spatial transitions across multiple clusters. Spatial neighborhood — report cluster composition spatial neighborhood defined k nearest spots, constrained distance threshold. Finally, can integrate Battlefield results back SpatialExperiment object analysis.

title: Battlefield

Battlefield operates simple spot-level table, first export data.frame four columns: spot_id: spot/barcode identifier (colnames(spe)) x, y: spatial coordinates (spatialCoords(spe)) cluster: cluster label provided user (column colData(spe)) cluster annotation can different names depending workflow (e.g., cluster, seurat_clusters, BayesSpace, etc.), user can specify colData() column used. load simulated Visium dataset (hexagonal grid) illustrate different functionalities Battlefield provides.  can acces basic information dataset using (grid type, distance threshold (radius) advised…)

title: Guidance for AI coding agents — Battlefield
text: Battlefield: low-level toolkit select spatial spots (fronts, margins, trajectories) spot-based spatial transcriptomics data (Visium / VisiumHD). Key data flow: raw SpatialExperiment / binned VisiumHD imports → cluster labels colData() → spatial coordinate tables (x,y) → selection helpers R/ produce ordered spot lines interfaces used vignettes downstream analyses. Core use case: Identify tissue regions (invasive margins, niche borders, cluster interfaces) downstream analyses like ligand–receptor studies (e.g., ligand-receptor interactions via BulkSignalR). Key algorithms: Bresenham line rasterization, k-NN neighborhood detection, grid type inference (square vs. hexagonal), layer classification, trajectory building via centroid--centroid paths. R version requirement: R ≥ 4.5 (base pipe |> syntax required).

text: Package metadata: DESCRIPTION (R >= 4.5, Bioconductor package dependencies). R/R-trajectory.R — geometry primitives (Bresenham), centroids, trajectory building. R/R-grid.R — grid type detection (square vs hexagonal), spacing estimation. R/R-border.R — cluster interface/border/core spot selection logic. R/R-layer.R — layer classification (border/intermediate/core) within clusters. R/R-neighbourhood.R — k-NN neighborhood composition analysis. R/R-spe.R — SpatialExperiment integration, adding selections colData. Data: R/data.R (documents included datasets: visium_simulated_spe, visiumHD_8um_simulated_spe, visiumHD_16um_simulated_spe). Tests: tests/testthat (uses testthat edition 3; organized module: trajectory, grid, frontline, layer, neighborhood, spe). forTest/R-build.R — full build, document, test, BiocCheck flow. forTest/R-visHD.R — realistic end--end VisiumHD import & selection example. forTest/R-test-*.R — interactive exploration scripts per module (R-test-traj.R, R-test-frontline.R, etc.). Main vignette: vignettes/Battlefield-Main.Rmd — primary user documentation examples four core workflows.

title: Guidance for AI coding agents — Battlefield
text: Pipe & verbs: Code uses base pipe |> (R 4.5+) dplyr verbs (mutate, filter, arrange, bind_rows, group_by, slice_*, pull, summarise). Use modern pipe syntax editing; avoid magrittr %>%. Spatial coords: x, y (numeric; required geometry helpers) Cluster identity: cluster column (factor/character/numeric; grouped cluster) Spot identity: spot_id (optional; used integrating SpatialExperiment) Selection metadata: interface, mode (added frontline/layer functions) Layer metadata: layer (added layer functions; values: “border”, “intermediate”, “core”) Directed pair: directed_pair (e.g., “3-4” added directed_cluster_interface_pairs()) Keep column names stable across refactoring; many helpers assume exact names. Keying deduplication: Coordinate deduplication uses .xy_key <- paste0(round(x), "_", round(y)). key identifies spatial duplicates; careful changing rounding logic keying scheme, intersection detection nearest-neighbor logic depend consistent keying. Numeric robustness: Functions defensively check edge cases (zero-length segments, empty clusters, insufficient neighbors) via stopifnot(). Examples: unit_normal_left(), build_one_trajectory(), bresenham_line(), detect_grid_type(). Pattern: Always validate .data.frame(df), presence required columns, non-empty rows, numeric coords. Preserve guards refactoring. Roxygen2 workflow: exports declared via roxygen tags. code changes, always run devtools::document() regenerate NAMESPACE man pages. Changes function signatures @export tags require step. Never manually edit NAMESPACE. Grid-aware code: Functions like detect_grid_type() estimate_spot_spacing() probe grid geometry. Square grids ~4 neighbors; hexagonal grids ~6. functions behave differently per grid type; always test square hexagonal layouts (using included test datasets). Layer depth control: Layer classification functions use intermediate_quantile (default 0.5) control depth intermediate layers relative distance border. Lower values (0.33) create narrow intermediate layers; higher values (0.75) create wider ones. tunable parameter users may adjust.
